title: India Tests Indigenous Kusha Missile in Push to Match S-400 and Patriot Systems
excerpt: DRDO's maiden flight test of the long-range surface-to-air missile places India among a select group of nations developing homegrown air defense shields.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • India's Kusha missile successfully tested, enhancing indigenous air defense capabilities.
  • Kusha system rivals S-400 and Patriot with a three-tier architecture.
  • Defence Minister highlights the importance of self-reliance in military technology.
  • Project Kusha aims to eliminate import dependency for long-range air defense.
  • India's defense exports reached a record ₹21,083 crore in 2023-24.

Maiden Test Marks Air Defence Milestone

India's Defence Research and Development Organisation on Wednesday successfully conducted the maiden flight test of the Kusha long-range surface-to-air missile from the APJ Abdul Kalam Island off the coast of Odisha. The test, conducted against an electronic target simulating a high-speed, high-altitude aerial threat, was successfully intercepted by the missile system, the Ministry of Defence said in a statement.

https://x.com/sidhant/status/2080285339839807642

The Kusha missile system is designed to neutralize a wide spectrum of aerial threats including fighter jets, cruise missiles, unmanned aerial vehicles, and large enemy aircraft across an extended range and altitude envelope. All weapon system elements — missiles, radars, and the command and control center — have been developed by DRDO laboratories and Indian industry partners, according to the official press release.

"The successful test-flight of Kusha marks an important milestone in Indian defence R&D, highlighting the capability in developing long range surface-to-air missile system, possessed only by a handful of nations."

— Rajnath Singh, Defence Minister of India

A Three-Tier Shield to Rival the S-400

Project Kusha is being developed as the backbone of India's future long-range air defence network. The system is planned as a three-tier architecture comprising M1, M2, and M3 interceptor missiles with engagement ranges of approximately 150 km, 250 km, and up to 350–400 km, respectively, according to the Times of India.

Once operational, the missile shield will be capable of engaging fighter aircraft, stealth platforms, drones, cruise missiles, precision-guided munitions, and certain classes of ballistic missile threats. The interceptors are expected to travel at speeds of around Mach 5.5 — roughly 6,800 km/h — supported by advanced radars, fire-control systems, and network-centric command infrastructure.

The system is designed to rival established platforms such as Russia's S-400 Triumf, which India controversially acquired in a $5.4 billion deal in 2018 despite the threat of U.S. sanctions, and the American MIM-104 Patriot system.

From Import Dependence to Indigenous Capability

The Defence Acquisition Council granted Acceptance of Necessity in September 2023 for the procurement of five squadrons of Project Kusha for the Indian Air Force. Bharat Electronics Limited is the principal industry partner for radar systems and overall integration.

The indigenous system is expected to integrate with the Indian Air Force's Integrated Air Command and Control System, enabling real-time tracking and engagement of multiple aerial threats simultaneously. Rajnath Singh emphasized that successful development would "eliminate the import dependency for such systems," signaling a shift away from reliance on Russian and Western military hardware.

Defence Secretary and DRDO Chairman Rajesh Kumar Singh monitored all activities during the launch and congratulated the teams involved.

Part of a Larger Defence Architecture

Project Kusha forms a key component of Mission Sudarshan Chakra, India's ambitious plan to establish a multi-layered national air and missile defence shield by 2035. The programme combines long-range interceptors with quick-reaction surface-to-air missiles, very short-range air defence systems, directed energy weapons, and indigenous ballistic missile defence capabilities.

India's Defense Export Surge
›₹21,083 crore Defense exports reached a record high.
›Shift towards becoming a net defense exporter.
›Focus on self-reliance in military technology.

For India's defence-focused diaspora and strategic analysts, the test signals a meaningful step in the country's push for self-reliance in advanced military technology. India already operates the S-400 system delivered by Russia, but Project Kusha would provide a fully indigenous alternative, reducing vulnerability to supply disruptions and sanctions pressure in an increasingly volatile geopolitical environment.

The test comes as India's defence exports reached a record ₹21,083 crore in the 2023–24 fiscal year, part of a broader drive to position the country as a net defence exporter rather than the world's largest arms importer.
